correctness.rationale: The layer-symmetric and antisymmetric Laplacians are L_C and L_C+2D. The former has nonzero eigenvalue product n² and the latter is positive definite for t>0, so the matrix-tree prefactor is n/2. The rank-three lemma and periodic delta-source recurrence give the specified I+uK_S (u=t−1) and normalized cyclic kernel with q=2−√3. Independently expanded the difference of the two 3×3 determinants and recovered the exact positive certificate. The contrast bracket 1+q^(2z)+(u/√3)(1−q^(2z)) exceeds 1−1/√3 for u>−1; the other nonzero factors have the required sign for y≥x+2. Gap balancing terminates by decreasing the sum of squared gaps. For the minimum, repeatedly transfer a unit from a nonlargest gap ≥2 to a largest gap; each is the inverse of a strict balancing move and terminates at (1,1,n−2). Permutations of three cyclic gaps are realized by rotations/reflection, so strictness and symmetry give all equality cases. At t=1 all placements tie. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_exact_checks.py prism. Independent full cofactors give (2480040,2432232) at n=9,t=2 and (147015,414421/3) at t=1/3 for balanced and consecutive placements, respectively. The frozen scripts were inspected, not run; the calculations support, not replace, the universal proof.

evidence: Write e_j for the elementary symmetric coefficients of the 3×3 kernel. The nonconstant balancing difference is u²(Δe₂+uΔe₃). The landmark result gives Δe₃>0; the pair kernel gives Δe₂>0. Together these already explain the u>0 sign.

For u∈(−1,0), ordering e₂ and e₃ separately is insufficient. The actual difference gives Δe₃/Δe₂=(1−q^(2z))/(√3(1+q^(2z)))<1, proving the missing weak-contrast inequality. The landmark result does not state this relation or optimize the shifted determinant.

At k=3 the same-date diffusion record has matching extremizer shapes and sign-insensitivity, but concerns the Kirchhoff index of a single resistive ring, with a different spacing function and no cubic competition.

It does not by its order claim imply weakening or the explicit all-contrast balancing factor. The other related objectives cannot substitute for this comparison.

evidence: The covariance kernel (μI+L_C)^−1 at μ=2 is K/2 for this prism. The indexed landmark theorem strictly balances its unshifted principal determinant; noisy observations and nonuniform screening are outside its scope.
The periodic finite ladder pseudoinverse can encode the unperturbed kernel; Klenke's straight infinite ladder has the same unit-weight geometric decay q=2−√3 without the periodic term.

originality.rationale: The closest distinct screened-cycle result already orders the principal determinant of the very same kernel under gap balancing, and contributes the cubic-coefficient comparison. The supported distinct claim is the full shifted determinant with exact strict finite-contrast ordering on both sides of t=1, especially the weakening side. The unweighted kernel and ordinary principal-determinant spacing order are not claimed as new. No earlier or same-date inspected independent statement was found to supply the full finite-contrast inequality.
residual_risks: A general diagonal point-impurity rearrangement theorem allowing both contrast signs could subsume the comparison. The broader search did not produce a material such source and this is not evidence of absence. Same-date labels alone establish no priority.

value.rationale: A natural discrete network-design problem has both exhaustive extremizers and an explicit strict local order, uniform over every size and all positive weights. Three defects introduce the first cubic interaction; the ratio bound explains why a sign reversal of the conductance perturbation cannot reverse the ordering even though it reverses the cubic term. This is not just computing the unweighted tree count or repeating a pairwise spacing law.
